articles.title: UEFA Nations League: Format, rules, promotion and relegation explained, and how it affects Euro 2028 qualifying
articles.summary: The 2026/27 UEFA Nations League is under way, with Portugal defending their title and England chasing a first triumph. But how does the competition work, what are the promotion and relegation rules, and what changes from 2028/29?
articles.body:
Portugal are the defending champions after beating Spain on penalties in the 2025 final , while England are looking to win the competition for the first time under Thomas Tuchel.

But there is more than a trophy at stake. Results can determine which division teams compete in during the next campaign, while performances could also have a significant impact on qualification for the European championship.

From how the format works to the promotion and relegation rules, here's everything you need to know about the UEFA Nations League.

The UEFA Nations League is an international competition involving Europe's national teams, designed to replace many of the traditional international friendlies with competitive fixtures.

First introduced in 2018, the tournament gives nations the opportunity to compete against teams of a similar standard, with promotion, relegation and a trophy on offer.

The competition is divided into four leagues - A, B, C and D - with League A containing the highest-ranked nations.

Portugal are the most successful team in the competition, having won the title twice, in 2019 and 2025.

France and Spain have also lifted the trophy, in 2021 and 2023 respectively.

The 2026/27 Nations League features 54 nations divided into four leagues.

Leagues A, B and C each contain 16 teams, split into four groups of four. League D consists of six teams, divided into two groups of three.

Teams play each opponent in their group twice, home and away, with points determining the final standings.

Three points are awarded for a win and one for a draw.

The top two in each League A group qualify for the quarter-finals, while the winners of those ties progress to the Nations League Finals in June 2027.

The bottom sides and teams finishing in other promotion and relegation positions will face a different challenge, with their performances determining which league they compete in during the next edition.

Promotion and relegation are central to the Nations League, giving teams something to play for throughout the group stage, regardless of their position in the rankings.

The four group winners in League B will be promoted directly to League A, while the four group winners in League C will move up to League B.

Teams finishing bottom of their respective groups also face the prospect of dropping down a division.

However, the 2026/27 campaign features a slightly different system as UEFA prepares to change the competition format for 2028/29.

The two lowest-ranked fourth-placed teams in League A will be automatically relegated to League B.

The other teams involved in the League A/B promotion and relegation battle will contest play-offs.

These will involve the four runners-up from League B against the two lowest-ranked third-placed teams and the two highest-ranked fourth-placed teams from League A.

The winners will play in League A in 2028/29, with the defeated teams competing in League B.

A similar system operates between Leagues B and C, with the four bottom-placed teams in League B facing the four runners-up from League C.

The winners will play in League B in the next edition, while the defeated teams will drop into League C.

When are the 2026/27 Nations League finals?

The league phase runs from September to November 2026, with the final two rounds of group matches taking place during the November international break.

The League A quarter-finals, alongside the League A/B and League B/C promotion and relegation play-offs, will take place between March 25 and March 30, 2027.

The Nations League Finals will then be held between June 9 and June 13, 2027.

The tournament will feature two semi-finals, a third-place play-off and the final, with four nations competing to be crowned champions of Europe.

Where will the Nations League final be held?

The 2027 UEFA Nations League Finals will take place between June 9 and June 13, 2027.

The host nation and stadiums are yet to be confirmed by UEFA. The four teams that progress through the quarter-finals in March will compete for the trophy, with the semi-finals, third-place play-off and final deciding the champions.

When is the Nations League knockout stage draw?

The UEFA Nations League knockout stage and play-off draw will take place at 12:00 CET on Friday, November 20, 2026, following the conclusion of the league phase.

The draw will determine the quarter-final and promotion/relegation play-off ties, with teams from the same group unable to face each other in the quarter-finals.

The eight teams finishing in the top two of the four League A groups will progress to the quarter-finals, which will be played over two legs in March 2027.

The four winners will then advance to the Nations League Finals in June 2027, with the semi-finals, third-place play-off and final deciding the champions.

What about the Home Nations and the Republic of Ireland?

The Nations League offers plenty of challenges for the five British and Irish nations, with England and Wales competing in League A, while Scotland, Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland are in League B.

England face Croatia and Spain, while Wales take on Norway and Portugal.

Scotland meet North Macedonia and Switzerland, Northern Ireland face Ukraine and Hungary, and the Republic of Ireland play Kosovo and Austria.

The results will determine who reaches the knockout stages, earns promotion or faces relegation.

What is changing in the Nations League from 2028/29?

The 2026/27 Nations League is the final edition to feature four divisions.

UEFA has approved a change to a three-league format for the 2028/29 competition, meaning League D will be scrapped.

All six teams currently competing in League D will automatically move up to League C.

The new structure will feature three leagues, each containing 18 teams split into three groups of six.

Teams will play six matches in the league phase, with the revised format designed to create a more streamlined competition.

The composition of each division will be determined by results in the 2026/27 Nations League.

League A will contain the eight quarter-finalists from the current edition, the two highest-ranked third-placed teams from League A, the four League B group winners and the four winners of the League A/B play-offs.

League B will include the two lowest-ranked fourth-placed teams from League A, the four defeated teams from the League A/B play-offs, the four third-placed teams from League B, the four League C group winners and the four winners of the League B/C play-offs.

League C will consist of the four defeated teams from the League B/C play-offs, the eight teams finishing third and fourth in League C, and the six teams currently in League D.

Does the Nations League affect Euro 2028 qualifying?

The Nations League will play an important role in the qualification process for Euro 2028, which will be hosted by England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland.

The final Nations League rankings will determine the seeding of nations for the European Championship qualifying draw.

The competition will also offer a potential second chance to reach the tournament through the play-offs.

Twenty-four teams will compete at Euro 2028. Twelve qualifying group winners and the eight best runners-up will secure automatic places, with the remaining runners-up entering the play-offs.

Nations League group winners who fail to finish in the top two of their Euro 2028 qualifying group will also be eligible for a play-off place.

Those places will initially be allocated to the best-ranked group winners from Leagues A, B and C. If additional places are required, they will filter down to the next-highest-ranked eligible teams.

The system means a strong Nations League campaign could prove decisive for countries who struggle in the traditional qualifying process.

articles.title: Windsor Park: Plans to increase stadium capacity to 23,750 part of UK's Women's World Cup bid
articles.summary: The planned redevelopment of Windsor Park to enable the stadium to host games at the 2035 Women's World Cup includes proposals to increase the capacity of the stadium to 23,750, according to a Fifa report.
articles.body:
The planned redevelopment of Windsor Park to enable the stadium to host games at the 2035 Women's World Cup includes proposals to increase the stadium's capacity to 23,750, according to a Fifa report.

A joint bid to host the tournament has been submitted by the governing bodies in England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.

The UK-wide bid is the only one put forward to host the tournament and is therefore set to be ratified at the Extraordinary Fifa Congress on 23 November.

Belfast's Windsor Park is the only stadium from Northern Ireland nominated as part of the bid, but in order to comply with the Fifa proposal that it could host games up until the quarter-final stage, the capacity of the venue must be increased from the current 18,500 capacity.

The Fifa report said that "further redevelopment is planned, including the increase in capacity" of Windsor Park up to 23,750 by 2035.

"These works are expected to enhance the stadium's suitability as a modern international venue," the report continued.

"The stadium authority has committed to implementing the necessary upgrades to achieve compliance with the minimum requirements."

Alongside the increase in capacity, other parts of the planned redevelopment to Windsor Park include the installation of "a hybrid‑grass system with tournament‑compliant field‑of‑play dimensions" and "an upgrade of the floodlighting system".

The Irish Football Association (IFA) has been contacted for comment.

The stadium was last redeveloped in 2015, when the IFA received £28.75m from the Northern Ireland Executive to bring the seating capacity up to 18,500.

Plans for Northern Ireland to host matches during Euro 2028 fell through after the government said it would not provide funding to redevelop Casement Park in time for the tournament.

Windsor Park is one of 19 stadiums that feature in the joint bid for the 2035 World Cup, with 14 based in England, two in Scotland and two in Wales.

The English based stadiums included in the bid are: Villa Park, The Amex, Ashton Gate, Elland Road, Hill Dickinson Stadium, Emirates Stadium, Selhurst Park, Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, Wembley, Etihad Stadium, St James' Park, City Ground, Stadium of Light and Old Trafford.

Easter Road and Hampden Park are the two Scottish stadiums put forward, with Cardiff City Stadium and Principality Stadium the two Welsh venues.

Brazil will host the 2027 Women's World Cup, while the United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica made the sole bid for the 2031 tournament.

The 2031 edition will be expanded to include 48 teams for the first time, up from 32.

articles.body:
As Sky Germany understands, Bayern Munich had considered making a potential move for Luka Vušković last summer.

However, in the end the German record champions decided against it because Kim Min-Jae ended up staying in Munich.

Bayern are still on pursuing Vušković, but any move has become unrealistic due to the exorbitant transfer fee.

As noted by the pay-TV channel, the 19-year old talent is already attracting interest from several top clubs within the Premier League.

One of which – Liverpool FC – are regularly monitoring Vušković and even have him on their shortlist for next summer.

With his contract at Brighton is valid until 2031 and no release clause available, the Croatian could cost a sum of up to €100million.

Ultimately, Vušković is deemed to be very happy under Fabian Hürzeler. However, his dream is to join La Liga giants Real Madrid one day.

articles.title: Lionel Messi eyes historic third straight MLS MVP award as USMNT star Cavan Sullivan becomes youngest-ever finalist
articles.summary: Lionel Messi has been named an MLS MVP finalist for the third consecutive season, while Philadelphia Union star Cavan Sullivan has become the youngest player...
articles.body:
Messi chases another piece of MLS history

Messi's place on the shortlist follows another prolific regular season for Inter Miami and he is bidding to become the first player in league history to win the award three times, having claimed it in 2024 and 2025. The Argentine scored 26 goals and provided 17 assists in 31 appearances, winning the Golden Boot and leading MLS with 43 goal contributions.

His challengers have strong cases of their own. Sullivan helped drive Philadelphia's surge after the World Cup break, while Mukhtar played a central role in Nashville's Supporters' Shield triumph. Evander finished with 31 goal contributions for Cincinnati, and Guilherme helped Houston return to the playoffs after missing out in 2025.

Nashville's B.J. Callaghan, St. Louis CITY SC's Yoann Damet and Vancouver Whitecaps' Jesper Sørensen are the finalists for Sigi Schmid MLS Coach of the Year.

Callaghan guided Nashville to a league-record 77 points, while Damet oversaw a 21-match unbeaten run across all competitions, the longest by an MLS club. Sørensen led Vancouver to the top of the Western Conference with a club-record 64 points.

Nashville lead all clubs with six finalists across the announced categories. Andy Najar, Jeisson Palacios and Maxwell Woledzi account for the entire Defender of the Year shortlist, while Brian Schwake is in contention for Goalkeeper of the Year.

Sullivan also shortlisted for Young Player of the Year

Sullivan's breakthrough campaign also earned him a place among the Young Player of the Year finalists, alongside Red Bull New York teammates Julian Hall and Adri Mehmeti.

The Union midfielder finished the regular season with nine goals and 14 assists, setting an MLS record for goal contributions by a teenager as Philadelphia secured a playoff berth. Hall and Mehmeti also enjoyed breakout seasons, with all three players earning USMNT call-ups.

articles.title: Cisse targeted by Arsenal, Brighton and more as Milan raise price to €60m
articles.summary: Milan forward Alphadjo Cisse is attracting interest from the Premier League, as Arsenal reportedly pursued him after Brighton and Hove Albion, with others fo...
articles.body:
Milan forward Alphadjo Cisse is attracting interest from the Premier League, as Arsenal reportedly pursued him after Brighton and Hove Albion, with others focused on the €60m talent.

The versatile figure just celebrated his 20 th birthday and is having a remarkable debut top flight campaign, scoring five goals in nine Serie A appearances, plus three in only four Europa League matches.

ITALY – NOVEMBER 8: Alphadjo Cissé of Milan (left) and Kingsley Ehizibue of Genoa vie for the ball during the Serie A match between Genoa CFC and AC Milan at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on November 8, 2026 in Genoa, Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images)

There had already been suggestions from Fabrizio Romano's Italian-language YouTube Channel earlier this week that Brighton and Hove Albion had made a verbal approach for the player.

However, Milan turned it down outright, confident that Cisse will keep going from strength to strength, especially after receiving his first senior Italy call-up for the Nations League .

ITALY – OCTOBER 28: Alphadjo Cisse of AC Milan celebrates scoring his team's second goal during the Serie A match between AC Milan and Bologna FC at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 28, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Now Tuttomercatoweb claim that Arsenal are among several other Premier League sides who have also set their sights on the Italian talent.

It is pushing the price tag higher and higher, already hitting circa €60m just a few months into his first top flight campaign.

TURIN, ITALY – AUGUST 23: Alphadjo Cisse of AC Milan scores his team's first goal during the Serie A match between Torino FC and AC Milan at Stadio Olimpico Grande Torino on August 23, 2026 in Turin, Italy. (Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

A product of the Hellas Verona youth academy, he was sold to Milan in February 2026 for €8.4m, but remained on loan in Serie B with Catanzaro to continue his development last season.

MLS has announced finalists for its year-end awards and after a record-breaking regular season , Nashville SC leads the charge.

Five Nashville SC players were named award finalists, more than any other club, while B.J. Callaghan was named a finalist for Coach of the Year.

articles.title: Ole Miss RB Kewan Lacy reportedly expected to miss rest of season in aftermath of latest shoulder injury
articles.summary: Lacy dislocated his left shoulder at Texas on Oct. 24 and hasn't played since.
articles.body:
Ole Miss is coming off a sobering 42-7 loss No. 1 Georgia, has dropped to No. 19 in the College Football Playoff rankings and reportedly won't be getting its leading rusher back this season.

Star running back Kewan Lacy is expected to miss the rest of the season due to injury, On3's Pete Nakos reported Thursday .

Lacy dislocated his left shoulder during a 34-27 loss at then-No. 19 Texas on Oct. 24 and hasn't played since. He had offseason surgery on that shoulder, per On3 . The junior suffered a different shoulder injury earlier in the season that caused him to miss time as well.

Thursday's news signifies that all three of the EA Sports College Football 27 cover athletes — Lacy, Miami wide receiver Malachi Toney and Oregon quarterback Dante Moore — appear to be out for at least the regular season.

Toney, though, could return for the CFP if he recovers in time from midseason ankle surgery.

As for Lacy, he appeared in six of the Rebels' nine games this season. Along the way, he piled up 388 rushing yards on 78 carries, averaging 5 yards a tote. He found the end zone five times on the ground.

He entered the 2026 campaign as one of the nation's biggest names. Last season, the 5-foot-11, 205-pound back was an All-American and a finalist for the Doak Walker Award, which is given annually to the best RB in college football.

In what was his first go-round at Ole Miss — following his transfer from Missouri — Lacy amassed a nation-leading 306 rushing attempts. He ranked third in the country with 1,567 rushing yards. And his 24 rushing touchdowns were good for the second most in the FBS during the 2025 season.

Lacy, along with quarterback Trinidad Chambliss, was instrumental in the Rebels making a run to the CFP semifinals, where they fell short at the Fiesta Bowl to eventual national runner-up Miami.

This fall, Ole Miss (6-3) will wrap its regular season with games against Oklahoma, FCS Wofford and Mississippi State.

In Lacy's absence, the Rebels have turned to Makhi Frazier and Shekai Mills-Knight at the running back position.

Lacy will be eligible to declare for next's year NFL Draft. In Eric Edholm's latest Big Board for Yahoo Sports , Lacy is ranked as the No. 46 overall prospect in the 2027 class.

articles.title: Examining the biggest issues behind Ohio State football's consecutive losses
articles.summary: Ohio State's problems extend beyond injury to quarterback Julian Sayin. Here's how issues across the roster have contributed to two straight losses.
articles.body:
Ohio State is in unfamiliar territory following consecutive losses .

The two-game skid leaves the Buckeyes in their first regular season with three losses since 2011.

The injury to Julian Sayin in October marked a turning point, but the Buckeyes' issues in recent weeks have extended beyond the loss of their starting quarterback.

Both sides of the ball, as well as special teams, have been fragile as Ohio State teeters on the edge of the College Football Playoff race .

Here's what's gone wrong during the Buckeyes' rare slide:

Ohio State's defense has gone from a strength to a vulnerability in a matter of weeks.

The Buckeyes have surrendered 35.5 points per game during their skid after allowing just 13.4 points over the first seven games. Both Oregon and USC burned Ohio State for big plays, accounting for nine of 24 gains of 20 or more yards given up by the Buckeyes.

The chunk plays not only flipped the field, but also ended in the end zone. Oregon running back Dierre Hill Jr. ran for a 48-yard touchdown, while USC wide receiver Trent Mosley made a 69-yard touchdown the previous week.

It wasn't until Ohio State's trip to USC that the defense had allowed a play longer than 40 yards this year.

"The explosives are something that we've got to eliminate," defensive coordinator Matt Patricia said. "Those plays that we haven't really given up change everything, the rhythm of the game, the outlook and maybe some of the calls that come after that."

Some of the breakdowns have emerged with Patricia seeking to make his side of the ball more aggressive. The Buckeyes have increased their blitz rate from 31% in the first two games to 48% over the past seven, according to Pro Football Focus. The uptick coincided with their loss at Texas in September.

But they have rarely been rewarded for taking more chances, leaving their back end more exposed. USC beat the Buckeyes' five-man blitz when quarterback Jayden Maiava found Mosley on a screen that turned into his 69-yard touchdown on the second play from scrimmage.

Oregon picked up the blitz as well when quarterback Dylan Raiola threw two touchdown passes, including a screen to Brandon Smith that went for 15 yards.

Neither Maiava nor Raiola was sacked by Ohio State. They were under pressure on just 25% of their dropbacks, per PFF.

While the Buckeyes' pass rush made a difference late in their win at Indiana on Oct. 17, it's had a limited impact by and large. They have managed just 11 sacks in nine games, a total that ranked 120 th in the Football Bowl Subdivision through Week 10.

Patricia said quarterbacks have had quick triggers, but they needed to identify more opportunities to affect them.

"We've got to just keep finding ways to get to the quarterback in those pass situations," Patricia said, "and really take a look at all of it."

Blitzes are not the only instances in which the Buckeyes have found themselves outnumbered downfield.

When Hill broke loose for his 48-yard touchdown run last week, it came against a front that overloaded the left side of Oregon's offensive line

The Ducks countered by pulling left tackle Fox Crader and left guard Tommy Tofi to the right side, opening a lane for Hill, who capitalized on their numbers advantage with a clear path to the second level.

Patricia pointed to a need for simplified communication and calls in order to avoid any misalignments.

"The fundamental philosophy of making sure that the alignments are quick and easy is something that we have to do a good job of," Patricia said.

The Buckeyes have not been productive enough in the ground game to overcome the absence of Sayin.

Their average of 4 yards per carry ranks 95 th in the FBS and is on pace to be the lowest in coach Ryan Day's eight seasons.

The struggles are a result of a variety of factors, beginning at the line of scrimmage.

Despite a bevy of experience on the offensive line, which included four of five starters returning from last season, the Buckeyes have averaged just 3 line yards per rush, ranking 73 rd in a weighted metric that estimates how many rushing yards are attributable to the offensive line, according to CollegeFootballData.com.

Injuries and illness have kept the Buckeyes from maintaining continuity up front. Ohio State has used five different starting offensive line combinations through nine games and has not started the same group in consecutive weeks since opening their Big Ten schedule against Illinois and Iowa.

Most of the instability has been at right guard and right tackle as Austin Siereveld and Phillip Daniels have each missed multiple games.

"It makes it difficult," center Carson Hinzman said.

But the frequent shuffling has not been the lone source of trouble. Hinzman pointed to missed assignments as also stalling the running game at various points.

"We've had so many plays that are blocked so well, but it's always one off," Hinzman said. "And then 25 one-offs kill you. It comes down to focus."

Ohio State's backfield has also missed Ja'Kobi Jackson, a seventh-year senior transfer from Florida who has been sidelined for three straight games after he reportedly underwent foot surgery.

Jackson had been the Buckeyes' most efficient running back. He averaged 0.24 EPA per rush attempt over six games, ranking second among Big Ten running backs, according to Game on Paper.

The Buckeyes have often fallen behind the chains on series.

"If you're on schedule on first own, it gives you an opportunity to be more balanced and creating a third down that's manageable," Day said.

Even when the Buckeyes are efficient and remain ahead of schedule while moving the ball on the ground, they have rarely been explosive.

Ohio State has only six runs of at least 20 yards, a total that ranks 120 th in the FBS. Only Michigan and Michigan State have gained fewer among Big Ten teams.

Bo Jackson leads the Buckeyes with three runs of 20 or more yards, but none of Ohio State's other running back has produced more than one.

Julian Sayin's injury exposed quarterback depth

When Lincoln Kienholz transferred to Louisville in January, it left the Buckeyes in need of a backup quarterback.

The most likely option seemed Tavien St. Clair , a former five-star recruit from Bellefontaine who was third string as a freshman in 2025.

Day's program has long stocked the quarterback room with blue-chip talent waiting in the wings.

Kyle McCord and C.J. Stroud were top-50 recruits who spent time as the No. 2 quarterback before becoming starters. Sayin was the No. 3 quarterback in 2024 before beating out Kienholz for the starting job last year.

But St. Clair didn't slide up. He was surpassed on the depth chart by Luke Fahey in preseason training camp.

It ultimately thrust Fahey, who lacked a similar recruiting pedigree as a three-star freshman , into a bigger role sooner than expected.

"It's something we have to make sure that we're prepared for," Day said, "because this is not about Luke Fahey, because Luke Fahey's trying his tail off, but, like any position, when someone goes down, we have to be able to keep the standard and expectation the same thing."

Sayin set a high bar for any replacement, especially pushing the ball downfield.

In his second season as the Buckeyes' starting quarterback, he averaged 10.5 yards per pass attempt, the second-most in the FBS among qualifying passers. He also completed 54.5% of passes traveling at least 20 yards through the air, per Pro Football Focus.

Fahey has averaged 7 yards per pass attempt with a completion percentage of 31.3% on deep passes in his two starts against Oregon and USC.

The drop-off reflects the reality of turning things over from a Heisman Trophy finalist to a freshman in the middle of the year.

Special teams have narrowed already-thin margins

While special teams struggles have persisted for years, they have been pronounced amid a more difficult schedule this fall.

Consider each of the Buckeyes' three losses.

Kicker Connor Hawkins missed a 45-yard field goal attempt at Texas in September that would have put Ohio State ahead by two scores with just over four minutes left.

At USC, the Buckeyes allowed Trent Mosley to return a punt 44 yards in the first quarter after their coverage overran him downfield.

Mosley not only flipped the field, but a late hit by defensive end Beau Atkinson allowed the Trojans to begin their series at Ohio State's 31-yard line, putting them in position to take a 14-3 lead.

Then there was Oregon's fake punt that picked up 30 yards late in the second quarter and swung momentum as the Ducks followed with 35 of their 38 unanswered points.

The problems culminated in the firing of special teams coordinator Robby Discher on Nov. 9. It was the first time Day let go of an assistant during the season.

The issues in the third phase might pale in comparison to others on offense or defense, but they have made it more difficult for Ohio State to prevail in close games.

Joey Kaufman covers Ohio State football for The Columbus Dispatch. Email him at jkaufman@dispatch.com and follow him on @joeyrkaufman on X.

articles.title: Reeling Oregon Ducks remain positive, committed to the grind
articles.summary: Players say the team maintains composure and connection despite two upset losses, with Nebraska visiting Autzen Stadium on Saturday night.
articles.body:
EUGENE — The 2026 season is on the verge of completely unraveling for the Oregon Ducks . One more loss, and any shred of postseason hopes would be extinguished.

Yet even after two upset losses and falling out of the rankings — despite starting the season at No. 2 — the Ducks (3-2, 1-1 Big Ten) remain focused, together and committed to salvaging the season.

"One thing I really love is the way the people in the locker room have been responding to this adversity," sophomore cornerback Brandon Finney Jr. said.

After his team's 17-15 loss to No. 12 UCLA on Saturday, Oregon coach Dan Lanning said the team would be measured by how it responds moving forward.

On Wednesday, he said the team has elevated its work ethic and embraced accountability.

"I've been proud of the way that they've worked," Lanning said. "I don't see a lot of hanging heads, right? I think that's challenging, too, especially when you're young, to not lose a little bit of gusto and not lose a little bit of belief."

The Ducks, who host Nebraska (5-1, 2-1) at 8 p.m. Saturday, responded well to adversity following a 39-31 loss at Oklahoma State on Sept. 12. Oregon won its next two games, including a 41-27 win at USC on Sept. 26.

That victory seemed to give the Ducks a fresh start. But two weeks later, they lost to the Bruins and dropped out of the rankings.

Now, Oregon must run the table to have a legitimate shot at the College Football Playoff, which seemed like a given for a team that returned most of its starters from last year's semifinal squad.

It's not uncommon for teams with grand expectations to unravel in tough times. So far, that hasn't happened.

"The team is very connected and maintains its composure whether we're winning or losing," punter Bailey Ettridge said. "We haven't let the losses last week and against Oklahoma State bring us down. I think we've handled them well."

Wide receiver Dakorien Moore said the team is filled with players who came to Oregon to win and be great. He added that the team's goals remain attainable, and team leaders have worked to encourage togetherness and mutual trust.

"If you can't trust your teammate, then everything ain't going to form in the way that it's supposed to," he said.

This also means trusting the process, the plan and the team's goal to get better instead of blaming one another.

"Everybody knows what we want to attack this next week, being that Nebraska is a good team," he said.

The outside noise has been deafening. To say that many Oregon fans have melted down on social media would be an understatement.

Virtually all of the players have social media accounts. Moore said he is active on social media but ignores negativity.

Finney said he isn't very active on social media and doesn't care what people say outside the program.

"Why would I let your opinion inflict me or my thoughts on my performance or my thoughts on our performance," he said. "Because people are going to be there when you're doing good, when you're bad; when you're doing bad, they're going to leave you."

For that reason, the team lives by the motto F.E.B.U., which stands for "Forget Everyone But Us".

"F.E.B.U. is a true statement that we all follow," Finney said. "… Just back to work. We got to figure out what we did wrong, go to the doctor, and just get back to work."

Fifth-year linebacker Devon Jackson said before the season that his main goal was team-driven — winning the national title.

"At the end of the year, what happens, happens, but I promise if we focus on the day and focus on one game at a time, we will be okay," Jackson said.

On Saturday, the Ducks' defense played one of its best games of the season, while the offense played its worst without starting quarterback Dante Moore , who remains in concussion protocol.

On teams that lack closeness, such a contrast can cause issues. But that is not the case with Oregon.

"I mean, we're all in this together," Jackson said. "It's not like, the defense won the game and offense lost, or special teams won or lost. We all lost together and we all win together. So, we got each other's back no matter what."

Jackson said that after Saturday's loss, he and senior center Iapani Laloulu talked for 20 minutes about the team. He told Laloulu that he didn't care what was going on with the offense; the defense had its back.

"I wouldn't trade that group with anybody else in the country despite what other people may think," Jackson said. "And we're going to continue to lean on each other because it's we all we got and we all we need."

Realistically, Oregon can't expect much sympathy from outsiders. The Ducks have top-notch facilities, infinite uniform options, a roster with an estimated payroll of $50 million , and a coach who isn't afraid to speak his mind, as Lanning did after beating the Trojans.

Many in the football world certainly wouldn't mind seeing Oregon fall.

"Ain't nobody going to feel sorry for us," linebacker Matayo Uiagalelei said. "So just came back in the next day with the mindset ready to work."
